Type declaration; no runtime value.

### Public members

#### `postMessage`

Transfer an execution envelope or result; structured-clone failures may throw.

Parameters:

- `value`: Structured-cloneable message envelope.

Returns: Completes without a value after the requested side effect.

Example:

```typescript
import type { ComputeWorkerPort } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute';
export function postCompute(worker: ComputeWorkerPort, id: number, pluginId: string, action: string, payload: unknown) {
 worker.postMessage({ id, request: { pluginId, action, payload } });
}
```


#### `addEventListener`

Register a message/error listener for the worker lifetime.

Parameters:

- `type`: Message/error event name.
- `listener`: Synchronous snapshot listener called on each published state.

Returns: Completes without a value after the requested side effect.

Example:

```typescript
import type { ComputeWorkerPort } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute';
export async function listenWhile(worker: ComputeWorkerPort, work: () => Promise<void>, received: (value: unknown) => void) {
 const listener = (event: { data: unknown }) => received(event.data);
 worker.addEventListener('message', listener);
 try { await work(); } finally { worker.removeEventListener('message', listener); }
}
```


#### `removeEventListener`

Remove the same listener during executor cleanup.

Parameters:

- `type`: Message/error event name.
- `listener`: Synchronous snapshot listener called on each published state.

Returns: Completes without a value after the requested side effect.

Example:

```typescript
import type { ComputeWorkerPort } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute';
export async function observeWorker(worker: ComputeWorkerPort, work: () => Promise<void>, received: (value: unknown) => void) {
 const listener = (event: { data: unknown }) => received(event.data);
 worker.addEventListener('message', listener);
 try { await work(); } finally { worker.removeEventListener('message', listener); }
}
```


#### `terminate`

Stop the worker; executor calls this on close, cancellation, timeout or failure.

Returns: Completes without a value after the requested side effect.

Example:

```typescript
import type { ComputeWorkerPort } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute';
export function disposeOwnedWorker(worker: ComputeWorkerPort) { worker.terminate(); }
```

<a id="api-createFileDownloader"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `createFileDownloader`

Chooses one file-saving destination and converts validation or adapter errors into failure data.

The host supplies the native adapter; a failed native save never silently changes destination.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function createFileDownloader(options?: {
    native?: NativeFileSaver;
    web?: NativeFileSaver;
    maxBytes?: number;
}): (data: Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer | Blob, save: SaveFileOptions) => Promise<SaveFileResult>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{     native?: NativeFileSaver;     web?: NativeFileSaver;     maxBytes?: number; }` | No | Optional native/web adapters and positive maxBytes limit, defaulting to 104857600 bytes; native takes precedence. |

### Returns

`(data: Uint8Array \| ArrayBuffer \| Blob, save: SaveFileOptions) => Promise<SaveFileResult>`

An async saver accepting bytes/ArrayBuffer/Blob and SaveFileOptions, resolving SaveFileResult even on adapter failure.

### Remarks

No fallback follows native failure. Browser success means the download was initiated, not durably written. Blob conversion allocates memory; native/web adapters own persistence and prompts.

### Errors and rejections

Error if maxBytes is not a positive safe integer at construction.

### Public members

#### `options.native`

Optional native adapter; selected before web and never silently retried in another destination.


#### `options.web`

Optional web save adapter, used only when native is absent.


#### `options.maxBytes`

Positive safe byte limit; defaults to 104857600 (100 MiB).



### Example

```typescript
import { createFileDownloader } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client';
const download = createFileDownloader();
export async function saveReport() {
 return download(new TextEncoder().encode('name\nSample\n'), { filename: 'report.csv', contentType: 'text/csv' });
}
```


<a id="api-createHttpPluginExecutor"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `createHttpPluginExecutor`

Creates a cookie-authenticated JSON POST transport for plugin operations.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client/plugin-execution`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function createHttpPluginExecutor(options: {
    endpoint: string;
    fetch?: typeof fetch;
    headers?: () => Record<string, string>;
}): PluginExecutor;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{     endpoint: string;     fetch?: typeof fetch;     headers?: () => Record<string, string>; }` | Yes | HTTPS endpoint without credentials/query/fragment; optional fetch and per-request headers callback. |

### Returns

`PluginExecutor`

An executor resolving parsed JSON, with pluginId/action appended as encoded path segments.

### Remarks

Host must enforce session, CSRF, tenant and operation permissions. Requests use include credentials, no-store and redirect:error; caller signal is forwarded. There are no retries or fallback destinations.

### Errors and rejections

Invalid endpoint throws immediately; returned executor rejects on header/serialization/fetch/JSON errors or non-OK HTTP status.

### Public members

#### `options.endpoint`

Credential-free HTTPS execution URL without query or fragment.


#### `options.fetch`

Optional fetch implementation; defaults to global fetch.


#### `options.headers`

Optional callback returning current host session/CSRF headers for each request.



### Example

```typescript
import { createHttpPluginExecutor } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/plugin-execution';
const execute = createHttpPluginExecutor({ endpoint: 'https://app.example.com/api/execute' });
export const readReport = () => execute({ pluginId: 'reports', action: 'read', payload: { id: 'sample' } });
```

The native command must independently resolve identity and enforce operation permissions.

```typescript
declare function createInvokePluginExecutor(invoke: (command: string, args: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<unknown>): PluginExecutor;
```

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invoke` | `(command: string, args: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<unknown>` | Yes | Installed native bridge that independently resolves identity and checks operation permissions. |

### Returns

`PluginExecutor`

An executor resolving the native result unless its signal has been aborted.

### Remarks

Aborting does not interrupt the native command; it discards the eventual response. Native side effects may already have completed.

### Errors and rejections

Returned executor rejects on aborted signals or native bridge rejection.



<a id="api-createKratosBrowserAuth"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `createKratosBrowserAuth`

Creates cookie-based Kratos OIDC login/logout actions with CSRF flow validation and redirect allowlists.

Browser OIDC uses Kratos cookies, CSRF and provider callbacks. No native API/token impersonation.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client/browser-auth`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function createKratosBrowserAuth(options: BrowserAuthConfig & {
    fetch?: typeof fetch;
    navigate: (url: string) => void;
}): {
    login(): Promise<void>;
    logout(): Promise<void>;
};
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `BrowserAuthConfig & {     fetch?: typeof fetch;     navigate: (url: string) => void; }` | Yes | BrowserAuthConfig plus host navigate callback and optional fetch; returnTo defaults to the current browser origin root. |

### Returns

`{     login(): Promise<void>;     logout(): Promise<void>; }`

login() and logout() actions resolving without a value after requesting navigation; failures reject.

### Remarks

Requires browser window when returnTo is omitted. Requests include cookies, disable caching/redirect following and time out after 15 seconds. Host must configure Kratos cookies/CORS and allowed identity-provider origins. Neither action confirms destination completion.

### Errors and rejections

Invalid configuration throws immediately; actions reject on transport/JSON failures, rejected flows or untrusted redirects; navigate errors propagate.

### Public members

#### `options.fetch`

Optional fetch implementation; defaults to global fetch.


#### `options.navigate`

Host navigation callback receiving a validated absolute redirect URL; no value is returned.



### Example

```typescript
import { createKratosBrowserAuth } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/browser-auth';
export const auth = createKratosBrowserAuth({ publicUrl: 'https://auth.example.com', provider: 'oidc', returnTo: 'https://app.example.com/', redirectOrigins: ['https://identity.example.com'], navigate: url => window.location.assign(url) });
// Call auth.login() or auth.logout() from a user action after configuring the host auth service.
```

### Errors and rejections

Invalid configuration throws; SDK failures and malformed profiles reject the corresponding action.

### Public members

#### `options.sdk`

Host-installed SDK instance; no provider credentials are returned by the wrapper.


#### `options.liffId`

Nonblank registered LIFF application identifier.


#### `options.redirectUri`

Credential-free HTTPS URI configured in the host identity provider.



### Example

```typescript
import { createLiffClient, type LiffAdapter } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/liff';
export async function connectLiff(sdk: LiffAdapter, liffId: string, redirectUri: string) {
 const client = createLiffClient({ sdk, liffId, redirectUri });
 await client.initialize();
 return { client, disconnect: () => client.invalidate() };
}
```


<a id="api-createPluginInvoker"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `createPluginInvoker`

Routes an explicitly configured plugin operation to its host-selected execution placement.

The host explicitly selects placement. A native failure never uploads data to a remote fallback.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client/plugin-execution`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function createPluginInvoker(options: {
    operations: Record<string, {
        placement: 'wasm' | 'browser-ai' | 'native' | 'server';
    }>;
    native?: PluginExecutor;
    server?: PluginExecutor;
    wasm?: PluginExecutor;
    'browser-ai'?: PluginExecutor;
}): (request: PluginExecutionRequest, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<unknown>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `{     operations: Record<string, {         placement: 'wasm' \| 'browser-ai' \| 'native' \| 'server';     }>;     native?: PluginExecutor;     server?: PluginExecutor;     wasm?: PluginExecutor;     'browser-ai'?: PluginExecutor; }` | Yes | Operation allowlist keyed pluginId:action and executors for wasm/browser-ai/native/server placements. |

### Returns

`(request: PluginExecutionRequest, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<unknown>`

An invoker resolving the selected executor result; operations are cloned when configured.

### Remarks

No failure triggers another placement. Native, worker and server adapters must independently enforce their trust boundaries. Cancellation is delegated after an initial abort check.

### Errors and rejections

Returned invoker rejects invalid identifiers, unconfigured operations, missing executors, cancellation and executor failures.

### Public members

#### `options.operations`

Explicit host operation allowlist; unlisted operations are rejected.


#### `options.operations.placement`

Explicit operation location; failures never choose a different location.


#### `options.native`

Optional native adapter; selected before web and never silently retried in another destination.


#### `options.server`

Optional server executor, responsible for current tenant and operation authorization.


#### `options.wasm`

Optional trusted WASM worker executor.


#### `options.'browser-ai'`

Optional trusted browser AI executor.



### Example

```typescript
import { createPluginInvoker, type PluginExecutor } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/plugin-execution';
export function routeReports(server: PluginExecutor) {
 return createPluginInvoker({ operations: { 'reports:read': { placement: 'server' } }, server });
}
```


<a id="api-createTenantModuleStore"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `createTenantModuleStore`

Creates an external store that discards obsolete tenant replies and removes module access while identity is loading.

Host supplies auth transport/events. Missing identity, fetch failure and stale responses never grant modules.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function createTenantModuleStore<T extends TenantContext>(load: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T | null>): TenantModuleStore<T>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `load` | `(signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T \| null>` | Yes | Host loader of verified identity and enabled module IDs; receives an abort signal when refreshed or cleared. |

### Returns

`TenantModuleStore<T>`

A store initially loading with no identity; loader and context-validation failures become snapshot.error.

### Type parameters

- `T`: Verified tenant context shape, extending the required tenant/user/module fields.

### Remarks

Call refresh initially and on host auth events; call clear immediately on logout. A refresh aborts the previous request. This store controls UI presentation; server authorization remains mandatory.

### Example

```typescript
import { createTenantModuleStore, type TenantContext } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
export async function connectIdentity(load: (signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<TenantContext | null>) {
 const store = createTenantModuleStore(load);
 await store.refresh();
 return { store, disconnect: () => store.clear() };
}
```


<a id="api-createWorkerPluginExecutor"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `createWorkerPluginExecutor`

Manages a lazy worker and rejects all pending computations when any call aborts, times out or crashes.

One worker per authenticated client scope. Cancellation terminates computation and pending calls.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function createWorkerPluginExecutor(createWorker: () => ComputeWorkerPort, timeoutMs?: number): {
    execute: PluginExecutor;
    close(): void;
};
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `createWorker` | `() => ComputeWorkerPort` | Yes | Factory for a trusted worker implementing the compute message protocol. |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | No | Positive safe integer timeout per call in milliseconds; defaults to 60000. |

### Returns

`{     execute: PluginExecutor;     close(): void; }`

An execute transport and close() that permanently closes the session and terminates its worker.

### Remarks

Use one executor per authenticated scope and close on logout/unmount. A failure terminates the shared worker and all pending calls; later calls can create a fresh worker unless closed. Payloads/results must be structured-cloneable.

### Errors and rejections

Invalid timeout throws immediately; execute rejects closed/aborted sessions, worker failures, timeouts or transfer errors.

### Example

```typescript
import { createWorkerPluginExecutor } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute';
export async function compute(workerUrl: URL) {
 const executor = createWorkerPluginExecutor(() => new Worker(workerUrl, { type: 'module' }));
 try { return await executor.execute({ pluginId: 'reports', action: 'sum', payload: [1, 2] }); }
 finally { executor.close(); }
}
```


<a id="api-createWorkspaceClientBindings"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `createWorkspaceClientBindings`

Bridges a typed plugin client through an isolated workspace session boundary.

Adapt a plugin's typed client through the shared authenticated snapshot/session boundary.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function createWorkspaceClientBindings<TClient, TData>(adapt: (tenantId: string, recordId: string, client: TClient) => WorkspaceClient<TData>, unwrap: (client: WorkspaceClient<TData>) => TClient): {
    Provider: ({ tenantId, sessionKey, client, children }: {
        tenantId: string | null;
        sessionKey: string | null;
        client: TClient;
        children: ReactNode;
    }) => react.FunctionComponentElement<WorkspaceProviderProps<TData>>;
    useClient: () => TClient | null;
};
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `adapt` | `(tenantId: string, recordId: string, client: TClient) => WorkspaceClient<TData>` | Yes | Converts a typed client and verified scope to a workspace transport. |
| `unwrap` | `(client: WorkspaceClient<TData>) => TClient` | Yes | Converts the guarded transport back to the typed plugin facade. |

### Returns

`{     Provider: ({ tenantId, sessionKey, client, children }: {         tenantId: string \| null;         sessionKey: string \| null;         client: TClient;         children: ReactNode;     }) => react.FunctionComponentElement<WorkspaceProviderProps<TData>>;     useClient: () => TClient \| null; }`

A Provider requiring tenantId/sessionKey/client/children and a useClient hook returning null outside its ready provider.

### Type parameters

- `TClient`: Plugin-facing client type.
- `TData`: Snapshot data carried through the shared session.

### Remarks

Keep adapters and raw client stable. The provider uses sessionKey as recordId and closes old sessions on scope change; host transports retain authorization and persistence responsibility.

### Example

```typescript
import { createWorkspaceClientBindings, type WorkspaceClient } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
const adapt = (_tenant: string, _record: string, client: WorkspaceClient<unknown>) => client;
export const { Provider, useClient } = createWorkspaceClientBindings(adapt, client => client);
```


<a id="api-createWorkspaceReactBindings"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `createWorkspaceReactBindings`

Creates an isolated workspace context with a provider that expires sessions on scope changes.

Creates typed React bindings for a workspace client without owning auth or data access.
Each call creates an isolated context, so unrelated plugin workspaces cannot cross-talk.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function createWorkspaceReactBindings<TData>(options?: WorkspaceSessionOptions): {
    WorkspaceProvider: ({ tenantId, recordId, sessionKey, client, children }: WorkspaceProviderProps<TData>) => react.DetailedReactHTMLElement<{
        role: "status";
    }, HTMLElement> | react.FunctionComponentElement<react.ProviderProps<WorkspaceClient<TData> | null>>;
    useClient: () => WorkspaceClient<TData> | null;
};
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `WorkspaceSessionOptions` | No | Session reply ordering; defaults to session-wide latest response. |

### Returns

`{     WorkspaceProvider: ({ tenantId, recordId, sessionKey, client, children }: WorkspaceProviderProps<TData>) => react.DetailedReactHTMLElement<{         role: "status";     }, HTMLElement> \| react.FunctionComponentElement<react.ProviderProps<WorkspaceClient<TData> \| null>>;     useClient: () => WorkspaceClient<TData> \| null; }`

WorkspaceProvider and useClient; the hook returns null outside a ready provider.

### Type parameters

- `TData`: Snapshot payload shared by the returned context and client.

### Remarks

The provider needs nonempty tenantId, recordId and sessionKey, shows status content until ready, and closes its session on cleanup. It performs no server authentication. See WorkspaceProviderProps.

### Example

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { createWorkspaceReactBindings, type WorkspaceProviderProps } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
const { WorkspaceProvider, useClient } = createWorkspaceReactBindings<unknown>();
export function HostWorkspace(props: WorkspaceProviderProps<unknown>) { return <WorkspaceProvider {...props}/>; }
export function ConnectionState() { return <p>{useClient() ? 'Connected' : 'Unavailable'}</p>; }
```


<a id="api-createWorkspaceSession"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `createWorkspaceSession`

Wraps a workspace transport with session lifetime and tenant/resource response checks.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function createWorkspaceSession<TData>(tenantId: string, recordId: string, source: WorkspaceClient<TData>, options?: WorkspaceSessionOptions): {
    close: () => void;
    client: {
        load: () => Promise<WorkspaceSnapshot<TData>>;
        execute: (operation: string, input: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<WorkspaceSnapshot<TData>>;
    };
};
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tenantId` | `string` | Yes | Verified tenant ID expected on every response. |
| `recordId` | `string` | Yes | Resource/session record ID expected on every response. |
| `source` | `WorkspaceClient<TData>` | Yes | Host transport responsible for current authentication and authorization. |
| `options` | `WorkspaceSessionOptions` | No | Response ordering scope; defaults to one latest reply for the entire session. |

### Returns

`{     close: () => void;     client: {         load: () => Promise<WorkspaceSnapshot<TData>>;         execute: (operation: string, input: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<WorkspaceSnapshot<TData>>;     }; }`

A guarded client plus close(), which invalidates pending responses without cancelling the underlying transport.

### Type parameters

- `TData`: Payload shape supplied by the host snapshot transport.

### Remarks

Session operations propagate transport errors and reject after close, when superseded, or for foreign tenant/record responses. Returned snapshots are cloned; server side effects can already have committed when a response is rejected.

### Example

```typescript
import { createWorkspaceSession, type WorkspaceClient } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
export async function readWorkspace(tenantId: string, recordId: string, client: WorkspaceClient<unknown>) {
 const session = createWorkspaceSession(tenantId, recordId, client);
 try { return await session.client.load(); }
 finally { session.close(); }
}
```


<a id="api-fetchVerifiedComputeAsset"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `fetchVerifiedComputeAsset`

Downloads a compute asset and checks its bytes against a caller-pinned SHA-256 digest.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function fetchVerifiedComputeAsset(asset: {
    url: string;
    sha256: string;
}, request?: typeof fetch): Promise<ArrayBuffer>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `asset` | `{     url: string;     sha256: string; }` | Yes | HTTPS URL (HTTP allowed only for loopback) and lowercase 64-character hexadecimal digest. |
| `request` | `typeof fetch` | No | Fetch implementation; defaults to global fetch. |

### Returns

`Promise<ArrayBuffer>`

Verified asset bytes owned by the caller.

### Remarks

Requires Web Crypto. Fetch omits credentials, rejects redirects and disables cache; no size limit or timeout is imposed. Pin the digest from a trusted release manifest.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects invalid URL/metadata, non-OK response, digest mismatch or fetch/crypto failure.

### Public members

#### `asset.url`

Trusted asset URL; HTTPS required except HTTP loopback development.


#### `asset.sha256`

Pinned lowercase 64-character hexadecimal SHA-256 digest from a trusted release.



### Example

```typescript
import { fetchVerifiedComputeAsset } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute';
export function downloadPinnedAsset(asset: { url: string; sha256: string }) { return fetchVerifiedComputeAsset(asset); }
```


<a id="api-installComputeWorker"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `installComputeWorker`

Installs a worker message handler that runs only host-registered pluginId:action operations.

Worker-side allowlist. Host code supplies the actual WASM/ONNX handler, never a module URL from the payload.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function installComputeWorker(scope: {
    addEventListener(type: string, listener: (event: any) => void): void;
    postMessage(value: unknown): void;
}, operations: Readonly<Record<string, (payload: unknown) => unknown | Promise<unknown>>>): void;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scope` | `{     addEventListener(type: string, listener: (event: any) => void): void;     postMessage(value: unknown): void; }` | Yes | Worker-like message target and response sender. |
| `operations` | `Readonly<Record<string, (payload: unknown) => unknown \| Promise<unknown>>>` | Yes | Trusted allowlist of handlers; each receives request.payload and may return a Promise. |

### Returns

`void`

Completes without a value after registering the listener.

### Remarks

Install once for a worker lifetime; no uninstall handle is returned. Errors are converted to generic failed response messages. Payload validation and access constraints belong to the registered handler; payload module URLs are never loaded.

### Public members

#### `scope.addEventListener`

Register the worker message handler for this worker lifetime; no disposer is returned.

Parameters:

- `type`: Worker event type; installComputeWorker registers message.
- `listener`: Handler receiving the host event envelope; it remains registered for this worker lifetime.

Returns: Completes without a value after the host registers the handler; no disposer is exposed by this structural scope.

### Errors and rejections

Host listener-registration failures propagate synchronously.

Example:

```typescript
import { installComputeWorker } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute';
export function registerMessages(scope: Parameters<typeof installComputeWorker>[0], received: (payload: unknown) => void) {
 scope.addEventListener('message', event => received(event.data));
 // The owning host terminates this worker to end its listener lifetime.
}
```


#### `scope.postMessage`

Send a structured-cloneable result envelope back to the client.

Parameters:

- `value`: Structured-cloneable result/error envelope returned to the client worker executor.

Returns: Completes without a value after the message is posted; no client acknowledgement is implied.

### Errors and rejections

Host transfer or serialization errors propagate synchronously.

Example:

```typescript
import { installComputeWorker } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute';
export function replyWithResult(scope: Parameters<typeof installComputeWorker>[0], id: number, result: unknown) {
 scope.postMessage({ id, ok: true, result });
}
```



### Example

```typescript
import { installComputeWorker } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute';
export function install(scope: Parameters<typeof installComputeWorker>[0]) {
 installComputeWorker(scope, { 'reports:sum': payload => {
  if (!Array.isArray(payload) || payload.some(v => typeof v !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(v))) throw Error('Invalid values');
  return payload.reduce((sum, value) => sum + value, 0);
 } });
}
```

### Signature

```typescript
interface LiffAdapter {
```

Type declaration; no runtime value.

Structural interface accepted by

### See also

createLiffClient for a complete host integration example.

Initialize the installed SDK for the given liffId; rejects SDK setup failure.

Parameters:

- `options`: SDK initialization or redirect options supplied by the host wrapper.

Propagates host adapter or SDK failures; async methods reject their Promise.

Example:

```typescript
import type { LiffAdapter } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/liff';
export async function initializeInstalledLiff(sdk: LiffAdapter, liffId: string) {
 await sdk.init({ liffId });
 return sdk.isLoggedIn();
}
```


#### `init.options.liffId`

Registered LIFF application ID supplied by the host-installed SDK wrapper.

Synchronously report the SDK login state.

Returns: Whether the installed SDK has a current login.

```typescript
import type { LiffAdapter } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/liff';
export function loginState(initializedSdk: LiffAdapter) { return initializedSdk.isLoggedIn(); }
```


#### `login`

Request provider login using the configured HTTPS redirectUri; no value is returned.

Parameters:

- `options`: SDK initialization or redirect options supplied by the host wrapper.

Returns: Completes without a value after the requested side effect.

Example:

```typescript
import type { LiffAdapter } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/liff';
export function requestLogin(initializedSdk: LiffAdapter, registeredHttpsRedirectUri: string) {
 if (!initializedSdk.isLoggedIn()) initializedSdk.login({ redirectUri: registeredHttpsRedirectUri });
}
```


#### `login.options.redirectUri`

Host-approved registered HTTPS return URI used by createLiffClient when requesting login.


#### `logout`

Clear SDK login state; no value is returned.

Returns: Completes without a value after the requested side effect.

Example:

```typescript
import type { LiffAdapter } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/liff';
export function signOut(initializedSdk: LiffAdapter) { initializedSdk.logout(); }
```


#### `getProfile`

Resolve presentation profile data or reject SDK failure.

Returns: The current SDK presentation profile.

### Errors and rejections

Propagates host adapter or SDK failures; async methods reject their Promise.

Example:

```typescript
import type { LiffAdapter } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/liff';
export async function readProfile(initializedSdk: LiffAdapter) {
 if (!initializedSdk.isLoggedIn()) return null;
 return initializedSdk.getProfile(); // Presentation data, never authentication proof.
}
```


#### `isInClient`

Optional SDK capability reporting whether running within LINE; absence is treated as false.

Returns: Whether running inside LINE.

Example:

```typescript
import type { LiffAdapter } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/liff';
export function isInsideLine(initializedSdk: LiffAdapter) { return initializedSdk.isInClient?.() === true; }
```

```typescript
declare function loadGoCompute(options: {
```

### Returns

`Promise<(action: string, payload: unknown) => Promise<unknown>>`

An async action/payload invoker that refuses calls after an observed runtime rejection.

### Remarks

The host must install matching Go runtime imports, implement readiness, and manage lifetime; this helper provides no stop handle. A readiness callback that never settles leaves loading pending.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects instantiation/readiness failures; returned invoker rejects stopped runtime or propagated invoke failures.

### Public members

#### `options.bytes`

Verified model or WASM binary bytes supplied by the caller.


#### `options.runtime`

Official matching Go wasm_exec.js runtime installed by the host.


#### `options.runtime.importObject`

WebAssembly imports provided by the matching Go runtime.


#### `options.runtime.run`

Start the Go instance; rejection is recorded and causes subsequent invocations to fail.

Parameters:

- `instance`: Go WebAssembly instance instantiated with this matching runtime importObject.

Returns: Resolves without a value when the Go program finishes; an active program can keep this Promise pending.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects host runtime/trap failures; loadGoCompute records rejection and rejects subsequent invocations.

Example:

```typescript
import { loadGoCompute } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute';
export async function runInstalledGo(runtime: Parameters<typeof loadGoCompute>[0]['runtime'], instance: WebAssembly.Instance) {
 await runtime.run(instance);
}
```


#### `options.ready`

Host readiness handshake; must resolve only when the WASM entry points are usable.


#### `options.invoke`

Host invocation bridge for the installed runtime; rejection propagates.



### Example

```typescript
import { loadGoCompute } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client/compute';
export async function startGo(options: Parameters<typeof loadGoCompute>[0]) { return loadGoCompute(options); }
```


<a id="api-loadRecordReference"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `loadRecordReference`

Loads complete tenant-scoped reference candidates and recursively resolves labels from authorized catalogs.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react/record-workspace`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function loadRecordReference(reference: RecordWorkspaceReference, tenantId: string, source: WorkspaceClient<unknown>, signal?: AbortSignal, referenceClient?: RecordWorkspaceProps['referenceClient']): Promise<RecordReferenceCandidate[]>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `reference` | `RecordWorkspaceReference` | Yes | Catalog operation, list key and display fields. |
| `tenantId` | `string` | Yes | Verified tenant ID for all returned records. |
| `source` | `WorkspaceClient<unknown>` | Yes | Authorized catalog transport; recordId must equal reference.pluginId. |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal` | No | Optional cancellation signal invalidating the session. |
| `referenceClient` | `RecordWorkspaceProps['referenceClient']` | No | Required for nested catalogs; returns independently authorized transports. |

### Returns

`Promise<RecordReferenceCandidate[]>`

Candidate records and composed display labels, including all pages or an empty array.

### Remarks

At most 100 pages of 100 records per catalog and four nested reference levels are accepted. Sessions close after loading; pending transport requests are not cancelled. Duplicate IDs/cursors and uncertain truncation fail instead of returning incomplete choices.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects foreign/malformed responses, missing nested adapters, pagination/depth limits, cancellation or propagated transport failures.

### Example

```typescript
import { loadRecordReference, type RecordWorkspaceReference } from '@alneas/eaos-react/record-workspace';
import type { WorkspaceClient } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
export function loadChoices(tenantId: string, source: WorkspaceClient<unknown>) {
 const reference: RecordWorkspaceReference = { field: 'reportId', title: 'Report', pluginId: 'reports', listOperation: 'list', listKey: 'reports', displayFields: ['title'] };
 return loadRecordReference(reference, tenantId, source);
}
```

<a id="api-PluginClientRuntime"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `PluginClientRuntime`

Live host request and compute capabilities bound to one authenticated session.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`, `@alneas/eaos-react/plugin-runtime`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface PluginClientRuntime {
    tenantId: string;
    sessionKey: string;
    request(pluginId: string, path: string, input: unknown, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<unknown>;
    compute(pluginId: string, action: string, input: unknown, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<unknown>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tenantId` | `string` | Yes | Current verified tenant identifier. |
| `sessionKey` | `string` | Yes | Current authenticated session generation; replace on identity changes. |
| `request` | `Promise<unknown>` | Yes | Perform an authenticated plugin API operation; resolve response data or reject host failures; honor the signal when possible. |
| `compute` | `Promise<unknown>` | Yes | Perform a host-selected compute action; resolve result data or reject; authorization and cancellation are host-owned. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

createWorkspaceReactBindings for a complete host integration example.

### Public members

#### `tenantId`

Current verified tenant identifier.


#### `sessionKey`

Current authenticated session generation; replace on identity changes.


#### `request`

Perform an authenticated plugin API operation; resolve response data or reject host failures; honor the signal when possible.

Parameters:

- `pluginId`: Plugin identifier whose current permission must be checked.
- `path`: Host API operation/path.
- `input`: Operation input validated and authorized by the host.
- `signal`: Cancellation signal; honor it where possible and do not expose stale results.

Returns: The host API result.

### Remarks

Host resolves CSRF and verified session headers on every request.

### Errors and rejections

Propagates host adapter or SDK failures; async methods reject their Promise.

Example:

```typescript
import type { PluginClientRuntime } from '@alneas/eaos-react/plugin-runtime';
export function requestPlugin(runtime: PluginClientRuntime, pluginId: string, path: string, input: unknown, signal: AbortSignal) {
 return runtime.request(pluginId, path, input, signal);
}
```


#### `compute`

Perform a host-selected compute action; resolve result data or reject; authorization and cancellation are host-owned.

Parameters:

- `pluginId`: Plugin identifier whose current permission must be checked.
- `action`: Requested plugin action to authorize against current state.
- `input`: Operation input validated and authorized by the host.
- `signal`: Cancellation signal; honor it where possible and do not expose stale results.

Returns: The host compute result.

### Errors and rejections

Propagates host adapter or SDK failures; async methods reject their Promise.

Example:

```typescript
import type { PluginClientRuntime } from '@alneas/eaos-react/plugin-runtime';
export function computePlugin(runtime: PluginClientRuntime, pluginId: string, action: string, input: unknown, signal: AbortSignal) {
 return runtime.compute(pluginId, action, input, signal);
}
```

<a id="api-PluginGate"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `PluginGate`

Renders plugin children only when the current tenant snapshot permits the plugin.

Missing/stale identity fails closed through the existing tenant module store.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`, `@alneas/eaos-react/plugin-gate`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function PluginGate({ pluginId, children, fallback }: {
    pluginId: string;
    children: ReactNode;
    fallback?: ReactNode;
}): react.ReactElement<{
    'data-plugin': string;
}, string | react.JSXElementConstructor<any>> | react.DetailedReactHTMLElement<{
    role: "status";
}, HTMLElement> | react.DetailedReactHTMLElement<react.HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, HTMLElement> | null;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{ pluginId, children, fallback }` | `{     pluginId: string;     children: ReactNode;     fallback?: ReactNode; }` | Yes | pluginId identifies the plugin; children are authorized presentation; optional fallback replaces a denied state. |

### Returns

`react.ReactElement<{     'data-plugin': string; }, string \| react.JSXElementConstructor<any>> \| react.DetailedReactHTMLElement<{     role: "status"; }, HTMLElement> \| react.DetailedReactHTMLElement<react.HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, HTMLElement> \| null`

A plugin-marked div, loading paragraph, fallback div, upgrade message, or null for tenant-locked/unspecified denial.

### Remarks

Requires TenantModuleProvider; this UI guard never replaces host/server authorization.

### Errors and rejections

Error outside TenantModuleProvider.

### Public members

#### `argument1.pluginId`

Plugin identifier admitted by current host policy.


#### `argument1.children`

React descendants rendered within this component.


#### `argument1.fallback`

Optional denied-access content; undefined selects the built-in denial behavior.



### Example

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { PluginGate } from '@alneas/eaos-react/plugin-gate';
export function ApprovalEntry() { return <PluginGate pluginId="approval"><a href="/plugins/approval/workspace">Approvals</a></PluginGate>; }
```

Newer authorized response from a plugin-owned operation, for the already selected record only.

Load plugin-owned auxiliary views after the shared initial list request has completed.

<a id="api-saveInBrowser"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `saveInBrowser`

Starts an anchor download and schedules object URL cleanup.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`, `@alneas/eaos-react/client`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function saveInBrowser(bytes: Uint8Array, options: SaveFileOptions): Promise<SaveFileResult>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bytes` | `Uint8Array` | Yes | File contents copied into a Blob. |
| `options` | `SaveFileOptions` | Yes | Filename and MIME type; contentType defaults to application/octet-stream; desktop reveal/open flags are ignored. |

### Returns

`Promise<SaveFileResult>`

Success after clicking the anchor; no path or durable-save confirmation is available.

### Remarks

Requires browser document, Blob and object URL APIs. The anchor is removed immediately and URL revoked after one second.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects for invalid filename, unavailable document or browser API failure.

### Example

```typescript
import { saveInBrowser } from '@alneas/eaos-react/client';
export const saveText = () => saveInBrowser(new TextEncoder().encode('Hello'), { filename: 'hello.txt', contentType: 'text/plain' });
```

<a id="api-TenantModuleStore"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `TenantModuleStore`

Host-driven subscription and refresh contract for tenant module visibility.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface TenantModuleStore<T extends TenantContext> {
    subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void;
    getSnapshot(): TenantSnapshot<T>;
    refresh(): Promise<void>;
    clear(): void;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `subscribe` | `() => void` | Yes | Register a synchronous snapshot-change listener; returns its unsubscribe callback. |
| `getSnapshot` | `TenantSnapshot<T>` | Yes | Return the current stable immutable snapshot. |
| `refresh` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Abort the previous request, clear identity while loading and publish only the latest result; errors become snapshot.error. |
| `clear` | `void` | Yes | Abort pending loading and publish a nonloading anonymous snapshot; no value is returned. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### Type parameters

- `T`: Host value shape carried by this contract.

### See also

createWorkspaceReactBindings for a complete host integration example.

### Public members

#### `subscribe`

Register a synchronous snapshot-change listener; returns its unsubscribe callback.

Parameters:

- `listener`: Synchronous snapshot listener called on each published state.

Returns: An unsubscribe callback; call it during cleanup.

Example:

```typescript
import type { TenantModuleStore, TenantContext, TenantSnapshot } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
export async function observeWhile(store: TenantModuleStore<TenantContext>, work: () => Promise<void>, changed: (snapshot: TenantSnapshot<TenantContext>) => void) {
 const unsubscribe = store.subscribe(() => changed(store.getSnapshot()));
 try { await work(); } finally { unsubscribe(); }
}
```


#### `getSnapshot`

Return the current stable immutable snapshot.

Returns: The current stable snapshot.

Example:

```typescript
import type { TenantModuleStore, TenantContext } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
export function currentIdentity(store: TenantModuleStore<TenantContext>) {
 const snapshot = store.getSnapshot();
 return { context: snapshot.context, loading: snapshot.loading, error: snapshot.error };
}
```


#### `refresh`

Abort the previous request, clear identity while loading and publish only the latest result; errors become snapshot.error.

Returns: Resolves without a value after publishing the latest context or error.

Example:

```typescript
import type { TenantModuleStore, TenantContext } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
export async function reloadIdentity(store: TenantModuleStore<TenantContext>) {
 await store.refresh();
 return store.getSnapshot(); // Inspect error as well as context after completion.
}
```


#### `clear`

Abort pending loading and publish a nonloading anonymous snapshot; no value is returned.

Returns: Completes without a value after clearing identity.

Example:

```typescript
import type { TenantModuleStore, TenantContext } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
export function onHostIdentityRemoved(store: TenantModuleStore<TenantContext>) {
 store.clear(); // Called by the host after logout or identity loss.
}
```



### Example

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

A generic async (operation, input?) function resolving host data; its type argument is a caller assertion, not runtime validation.

### Remarks

Use within React under PluginRuntimeProvider. Scope changes/unmount abort the shared signal and invalidate replies. Host must honor cancellation where possible; completed side effects are not rolled back.

### Errors and rejections

Returned function rejects missing runtime, invalid plugin ID, expired session and propagated host errors.

### Example

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { usePluginApi } from '@alneas/eaos-react/plugin-runtime';
// Mount below PluginRuntimeProvider supplied by the authenticated host.
export function ReloadButton() { const execute = usePluginApi('reports'); return <button onClick={() => void execute('read', { id: 'sample' }).catch(console.error)}>Read</button>; }
```

<a id="api-UserGuide"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `UserGuide`

Renders structured repository-authored help as native HTML details without executing HTML content.

Static repository-authored document data, never executable HTML or fetched tenant content.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react/user-guide`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function UserGuide({ document, summary, initiallyOpen }: {
    document: UserGuideDocument;
    summary?: string;
    initiallyOpen?: boolean;
}): react.JSX.Element;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{ document, summary, initiallyOpen }` | `{     document: UserGuideDocument;     summary?: string;     initiallyOpen?: boolean; }` | Yes | Version-1 document, optional summary (default Japanese help title) and initiallyOpen flag (default false). |

### Returns

`react.JSX.Element`

A collapsible guide; unsupported link protocols render as plain inline content.

### Remarks

Requires React. The scrollable guide body is keyboard-focusable. Heading levels are shifted down by one, capped at h6. Pass trusted static document data, not tenant-authored executable content.

### Errors and rejections

Error for a document schemaVersion other than 1.

### Public members

#### `argument1.document`

Trusted static structured help document with schemaVersion 1.


#### `argument1.summary`

Details trigger caption; defaults to the bundled Japanese help title.


#### `argument1.initiallyOpen`

Whether the help starts expanded; defaults to false.



### Example

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { UserGuide, type UserGuideDocument } from '@alneas/eaos-react/user-guide';
const document: UserGuideDocument = { schemaVersion: 1, id: 'sample', locale: 'en', blocks: [{ type: 'paragraph', children: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Select a record to begin.' }] }] };
export function Help() { return <UserGuide document={document} summary="Help"/>; }
```

<a id="api-useWorkspaceClientAdapter"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `useWorkspaceClientAdapter`

Memoizes a plugin adapter for the current tenant, session and source client.

Keep a raw client adapter stable while the verified host scope is unchanged.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function useWorkspaceClientAdapter<T, U>(tenantId: string | null, sessionKey: string | null, client: T, adapt: (tenantId: string, recordId: string, client: T) => WorkspaceClient<U>): WorkspaceClient<U>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tenantId` | `string \| null` | Yes | Current verified tenant ID, or null. |
| `sessionKey` | `string \| null` | Yes | Current host session/resource key, or null. |
| `client` | `T` | Yes | Stable raw host client. |
| `adapt` | `(tenantId: string, recordId: string, client: T) => WorkspaceClient<U>` | Yes | Converts tenant/resource/client into a workspace client; receives empty IDs when scope is missing. |

### Returns

`WorkspaceClient<U>`

The adapted client, recomputed when any dependency changes.

### Type parameters

- `T`: Raw client shape.
- `U`: Adapted snapshot payload.

### Remarks

React hook; adapt must be stable and must fail closed for empty scope. The surrounding workspace provider determines readiness.

### Example

```typescript
import { useWorkspaceClientAdapter, type WorkspaceClient } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
export function useHostAdapter<T>(tenantId: string | null, sessionKey: string | null, client: WorkspaceClient<T>) {
 return useWorkspaceClientAdapter(tenantId, sessionKey, client, (_tenant, _resource, source) => source);
}
```


<a id="api-useWorkspaceTask"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `useWorkspaceTask`

Tracks one pending UI task and suppresses obsolete completion state after client changes.

UI-only single-flight guard. The host still owns authorization and durable execution.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function useWorkspaceTask(client: unknown, onFailure: () => void): {
    busy: boolean;
    error: string | null;
    setBusy: react.Dispatch<react.SetStateAction<boolean>>;
    setError: react.Dispatch<react.SetStateAction<string | null>>;
    generation: react.RefObject<number>;
    pending: react.RefObject<number | null>;
    run: (work: (generation: number) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>;
};
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `client` | `unknown` | Yes | Active transport identity; falsy values disable run. |
| `onFailure` | `() => void` | Yes | Called after a current task rejects, before storing its error message. |

### Returns

`{     busy: boolean;     error: string \| null;     setBusy: react.Dispatch<react.SetStateAction<boolean>>;     setError: react.Dispatch<react.SetStateAction<string \| null>>;     generation: react.RefObject<number>;     pending: react.RefObject<number \| null>;     run: (work: (generation: number) => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>; }`

Busy/error state and setters, generation/pending refs and run(work); skipped tasks resolve without running work.

### Remarks

React hook. Tasks are not cancelled on unmount/client change, and a single-flight guard is not server idempotency. work receives the generation to check before applying results.

### Example

```typescript
import { useWorkspaceTask } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
export function useReload(client: object | null, reload: () => Promise<void>, clear: () => void) {
 const task = useWorkspaceTask(client, clear);
 return { ...task, reload: () => task.run(async () => { await reload(); }) };
}
```

<a id="api-WorkspaceClient"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `WorkspaceClient`

Authenticated host transport for loading and executing workspace operations.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface WorkspaceClient<TData = unknown> {
    load(): Promise<WorkspaceSnapshot<TData>>;
    execute(operation: string, input: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<WorkspaceSnapshot<TData>>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `load` | `Promise<WorkspaceSnapshot<TData>>` | Yes | Load the current authorized snapshot; resolves a WorkspaceSnapshot or rejects transport/authorization failure. |
| `execute` | `Promise<WorkspaceSnapshot<TData>>` | Yes | Execute a named host operation with typed JSON-like input and return the resulting authorized snapshot; rejects host failures. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### Type parameters

- `TData`: Host snapshot payload; defaults to unknown.

### Remarks

Host transport for a bounded, optimistic-concurrency workspace.

### See also

createWorkspaceReactBindings for a complete host integration example.

### Public members

#### `load`

Load the current authorized snapshot; resolves a WorkspaceSnapshot or rejects transport/authorization failure.

Returns: The current authorized snapshot.

### Errors and rejections

Propagates host adapter or SDK failures; async methods reject their Promise.

Example:

```typescript
import type { WorkspaceClient } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
export async function readWorkspace<T>(client: WorkspaceClient<T>) {
 const snapshot = await client.load();
 return { tenantId: snapshot.tenantId, revision: snapshot.revision, data: snapshot.data };
}
```


#### `execute`

Execute a named host operation with typed JSON-like input and return the resulting authorized snapshot; rejects host failures.

Parameters:

- `operation`: Host operation identifier.
- `input`: Operation input validated and authorized by the host.

Returns: The next authorized snapshot.

### Errors and rejections

Propagates host adapter or SDK failures; async methods reject their Promise.

Example:

```typescript
import type { WorkspaceClient } from '@alneas/eaos-react';
export async function executeWorkspace<T>(client: WorkspaceClient<T>, operation: string, input: Record<string, unknown>) {
 return client.execute(operation, input); // Include the operation's required revision and validated fields.
}
```



### Example

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

<a id="api-WorkspaceNumberField"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `WorkspaceNumberField`

Renders a controlled required numeric input while preserving blank values as NaN.

Empty numeric input remains NaN, never an accidental zero amount.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react/workspace-fields`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function WorkspaceNumberField({ label, value, onChange, min, max, step }: {
    label: string;
    value: number;
    onChange: (value: number) => void;
    min?: number;
    max?: number;
    step?: string;
}): react.JSX.Element;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{ label, value, onChange, min, max, step }` | `{     label: string;     value: number;     onChange: (value: number) => void;     min?: number;     max?: number;     step?: string; }` | Yes | label/value/onChange with min=0, max=1000000000000 and step=any; onChange receives a number or NaN when cleared. |

### Returns

`react.JSX.Element`

A labeled numeric Input; nonfinite values render blank.

### Remarks

Requires React,

### Public members

#### `argument1.label`

Human-readable field caption.


#### `argument1.value`

Controlled field value; the host must update it in response to onChange.


#### `argument1.onChange`

Receives the parsed user input; update controlled state in this callback.


#### `argument1.min`

Numeric lower bound; defaults to 0.


#### `argument1.max`

Numeric upper bound; defaults to 1000000000000.


#### `argument1.step`

Numeric input increment string; defaults to any.



### Example

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { WorkspaceNumberField } from '@alneas/eaos-react/workspace-fields';
export function AmountField() { const [value, setValue] = React.useState(NaN); return <WorkspaceNumberField label="Amount" value={value} onChange={setValue}/>; }
```

<a id="api-WorkspaceSessionOptions"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `WorkspaceSessionOptions`

Controls which concurrent workspace replies supersede each other.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface WorkspaceSessionOptions {
    responseScope?: 'session' | 'operation-resource';
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `responseScope` | `'session' \| 'operation-resource'` | No | Session-wide latest reply by default; operation-resource keeps independent latest replies per operation and string input.id. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### Remarks

Adds lifecycle, stale-response and tenant/resource checks around a host client.
This is UI session state only; authorization remains server-owned.

### See also

createWorkspaceReactBindings for a complete host integration example.

### Public members

#### `responseScope`

Session-wide latest reply by default; operation-resource keeps independent latest replies per operation and string input.id.

Default: `'session'`.

### Remarks

Independent panels may retain replies from different operations/resources. Default: one latest reply for the session.

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

<a id="api-WorkspaceSidebar"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `WorkspaceSidebar`

Renders host navigation and identity controls using the shared collapsible sidebar.

Both generated and existing hosts use the same navigation and react-tools sidebar.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react/workspace-shell`, `@alneas/eaos-react/workspace-layout`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function WorkspaceSidebar({ tenantName, activePath, onNavigate, onLogout, user, footer, ...options }: WorkspaceNavigationOptions & {
    tenantName?: string;
    activePath?: string;
    onNavigate: (path: string) => void;
    onLogout?: () => void;
    user?: HeaderProps['user'];
    footer?: ReactNode;
}): react.JSX.Element;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{ tenantName, activePath, onNavigate, onLogout, user, footer, ...options }` | `WorkspaceNavigationOptions & {     tenantName?: string;     activePath?: string;     onNavigate: (path: string) => void;     onLogout?: () => void;     user?: HeaderProps['user'];     footer?: ReactNode; }` | Yes | Navigation options, optional tenant/user/footer, activePath and host onNavigate/onLogout callbacks. |

### Returns

`react.JSX.Element`

A SmartSidebar; selecting links closes its mobile state before notifying the host.

### Remarks

Requires React,

### Public members

#### `argument1.tenantName`

Optional tenant heading; omitted or empty displays Workspace.


#### `argument1.activePath`

Current host router path used for active navigation styling.


#### `argument1.onNavigate`

Host route callback; receives the selected path after mobile sidebar is closed.


#### `argument1.onLogout`

Optional host logout callback; it must clear verified UI state and perform real logout.


#### `argument1.user`

Optional Header user presentation data; never used to derive API authority.


#### `argument1.footer`

Optional custom footer replacing the default identity/logout controls.



### Example

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { WorkspaceSidebar } from '@alneas/eaos-react/workspace-layout';
// Render within the host Appkit React SidebarProvider.
export function Sidebar({navigate}: {navigate: (path: string) => void}) { return <WorkspaceSidebar onNavigate={navigate}/>; }
```

<a id="api-WorkspaceTextField"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `WorkspaceTextField`

Renders a controlled labeled text input or textarea with native length and required constraints.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-react/workspace-fields`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function WorkspaceTextField({ label, value, onChange, multiline, required, max, type }: {
    label: string;
    value: string;
    onChange: (value: string) => void;
    multiline?: boolean;
    required?: boolean;
    max?: number;
    type?: string;
}): react.JSX.Element;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{ label, value, onChange, multiline, required, max, type }` | `{     label: string;     value: string;     onChange: (value: string) => void;     multiline?: boolean;     required?: boolean;     max?: number;     type?: string; }` | Yes | label/value/onChange plus multiline=false, required=false, max=200 characters and type=text; onChange receives the entered string. |

### Returns

`react.JSX.Element`

A label containing Input or Textarea.

### Remarks

Requires React,

### Public members

#### `argument1.label`

Human-readable field caption.


#### `argument1.value`

Controlled field value; the host must update it in response to onChange.


#### `argument1.onChange`

Receives the parsed user input; update controlled state in this callback.


#### `argument1.multiline`

Render a Textarea when true; defaults to false.


#### `argument1.required`

Native required constraint; defaults to false for WorkspaceTextField.


#### `argument1.max`

Maximum text length in characters; defaults to 200.


#### `argument1.type`

Native text input type; defaults to text.



### Example

```tsx
import * as React from 'react';
import { WorkspaceTextField } from '@alneas/eaos-react/workspace-fields';
export function NameField() { const [value, setValue] = React.useState(''); return <WorkspaceTextField label="Name" value={value} onChange={setValue}/>; }
```
